title: Bsd Saturation
objective: Implement honest genus-2/3 Mordell-Weil subgroup saturation and index certificates
references: Nils Bruin and Michael Stoll, The Mordell-Weil sieve: proving non-existence of rational points on curves
Samir Siksek, Infinite descent on elliptic curves

oracles: existing certified finite-field Jacobian invariant-factor maps
exact toy lattices with independently known saturation and index

handoff.summary: Adds an ordinary-Python, Wasm-safe saturation engine with internally replayed finite-reduction constraints, a classical bounded rational Mumford division search, exact basis/index chains, typed rank/index/torsion provenance, and structured unsupported/resource outcomes. Immutable result records replay all raw evidence and reject forged ranks, kernels, statuses, global claims, or full-Mordell-Weil flags. The result separately labels independence, full rank, ell-division obstruction, torsion-controlled free-quotient saturation, global index, torsion completion, and full Mordell-Weil determination.
risks: A failed bounded division search is intentionally unresolved unless a registered verifier accepts a typed theorem binding the replayed coefficient box to a global height/search bound.

The deterministic exhaustive finite-group-map fallback is deliberately capped at group order 512; larger residue groups use the existing certified sampled abelian-group implementation and its explicit operation/memory budgets.
Public Jacobian methods, strict-module registry entries, and forthcoming height/torsion adapters are integration-owned and intentionally not edited in this narrow lane.
next_steps: Wire HyperellipticJacobian.saturate lazily to saturate_subgroup and add saturation.py to pyrightconfig.json.
Connect certified genus-2/3 height lower bounds, exact torsion records, and rank/Selmer verifiers through the typed assumption registry.
Extend the bounded classical division envelope only when proved height-to-Mumford-coefficient bounds justify larger boxes.
